findings.assumptions: No additional conjectural assumptions are introduced. Triangle-freeness supplies trace(A^3)=0 and nonnegative deficit. The substantive external dependency is Lemma 4.3 of arXiv:2609.20225v2, whose statement and proof are supplied. Ordinary finite real spectral theory suffices for the remaining calculations.
findings.equivalence: Neither coefficient fifteen nor the asymptotic coefficient-three upper bound is equivalent to the exact root inequality. C5 excludes universal coefficients below three, but does not establish sharpness within sequences having vanishing relative deficit.
findings.mathematical_substance: The supplied candidate has a concrete, coherent proof chain: the least-eigenvector sign cut satisfies lambda(F)>=mu; bipartite editing gives D(G)<=3(m-mu^2)-2b; the trace-cube estimate gives m-mu^2<=5xi. Removing the two extreme eigenvalues then gives squared spectral remainder at most 6xi and the displayed asymptotic estimate. The analytical part-size enumeration establishes D(C5)=3. These support admission for independent proof acceptance, not root closure.
findings.necessity: This standalone branch is not a necessary reduction or exhaustive decomposition of the root. Its justification is the explicit quantitative consequence, not an asserted requirement that every root proof pass through it.
findings.novelty: The delivered comparison texts establish qualitative triangle-free editing and linear bipartite editing, rather than the proposed general bounds. Historical novelty and openness remain unverified: the packet reports six complete readings but supplies full texts for only three distinct comparators, and the underlying search records are not delivered.
findings.renewal_basis: No renewal is requested. The proposed two analytical moves consume the existing account, subject to the original aggregate 24-move, 24-run and one-worker limits; branch limits do not create a fresh allowance.
findings.root_connection: The proposal retains the root graph class, spectral deficit and edit functional. It investigates explicit weaker bounds and a lower-bound witness, without discharging or replacing obligation-000001.
findings.scope: The claim covers arbitrary finite order, disconnected graphs and isolates, with empty target parts permitted. Edgeless graphs are handled separately; division by lambda is restricted to lambda>0. The sequence conclusion follows from sqrt(xi)/lambda=sqrt((xi/m)/(1-xi/m)). No numerical computation is proposed or authorized.
findings.significance: If independently accepted, the theorem supplies a uniform linear modulus and a quantitative near-threshold refinement, separating existence of a finite coefficient from determination of the optimal universal coefficient. No stronger significance or priority claim is supported.

unresolved_objections.description: Any later resolved openness or historical-priority finding requires delivered, bound search records and complete readings of relevant comparators. In particular, the claimed readings of arXiv:2512.19395v1, 2511.15431v3 and 2608.24388v2 are not supplied here. Their reported completion cannot receive independent reading credit. This gap does not block the present analytical proposal.
